items.title: Two normalized spherical Poisson moments

source.anchor: Lemma A.1, Eq12 and proof (A1.SS1); applied in B.2.2 immediately before Eq24

The author applies HFT1.21 to h=1 and h=x1; the checked proof uses a separately identified mean-value/zero-flux route. No full Poisson representation theorem is claimed.

source.label: Lemma A.1: two normalized sphere moments

items.statement: For a uniform unit vector, the reciprocal radial denominator and its first-coordinate weighted version have the following finite expectations.
assumptions: \(n\ge2\), \(0<r<1\), and \(U=\zeta_1\) for a uniform \(\zeta\in S^{n-1}\subset\mathbb R^n\).

The literal law is \(\sigma=\iota_*(\tau(S^{n-1})^{-1}\tau)\), where \(\tau=\mathrm{volume}.\mathrm{toSphere}\) and \(\iota\) is the sphere inclusion. Its normalization and both integrability conclusions are derived internally.
The pinned source contains both \(n\ge2\) and a trailing \(n\ge3\). The \(n=2\) result is an explicit extension; the paper application and the selected-parameter consumer keep \(n\ge3\).

obligations.label: Both actual finite sphere expectations in LemmaA.1, with the explicitly disclosed n=2 extension.

assumption_deltas.source: 0<r<1 and U is the first coordinate of a normalized uniform Euclidean unit vector.
assumption_deltas.lean: Same strict r domain and first coordinate under the literal normalized volume.toSphere ambient pushforward.
assumption_deltas.reason: The canonical source-law correspondence already identifies this polar surface law; compact sphere positivity/continuity gives both L1 conclusions internally. No regularity, moment value, flux, representation or normalization premise is added.

assumption_deltas.source: Both expectations use negative real power and are finite.
assumption_deltas.lean: Both genuine L1 facts and real Bochner integrals of reciprocal positive real power.
assumption_deltas.reason: The actual denominator is strictly positive on the sphere support. Positive-base rpow_neg identifies the source formula. Measurable pushforward transfers L1 and integrals; off-support totalized division is immaterial.
